subject: science
passage: Many limpets, cone-shaped snails that cling to rocks along the shore, creep away from their resting places to scrape algae off the rock, often while the tide is in, yet they return to the very same spot before the water recedes. Over time, the rim of each shell and the rock beneath it wear into a precise fit, forming a shallow depression called a home scar. A limpet settled in its own scar seals tightly enough to keep from drying out at low ______ clinging anywhere else on the rock may lose far more water.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A limpet settled in its own scar seals tightly enough to keep from drying out at low tide" is an independent clause, and "one clinging anywhere else on the rock may lose far more water" could stand alone too. Adding the subordinating conjunction "whereas" makes the second part a dependent clause that expresses a contrast, and a comma correctly attaches it to the main clause.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is a comma splice: a comma alone can't join two independent clauses.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The period leaves "Whereas one clinging anywhere else on the rock may lose far more water" as a sentence fragment.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon must be followed by an independent clause, but "whereas one clinging … may lose far more water" is a dependent clause.
explanation.D: Correct. "Whereas" makes the second part a dependent clause, and a comma correctly attaches it to the independent clause.
